newsitem.title: USA: ConnexT, Puget Sound Energy sign 10-yr dea.
newsitem.headline: ConnexT, Puget Sound Energy sign 10-yr dea.

text.p: ConnexT Inc, a private Seattle-based utility services company, said Tuesday it has signed a 10-year contract to provide customer data and billing services for Puget Sound Energy.
The deal, serving Puget Sound Energy's nearly 1.4 million customers, is valued at $100 million over the life of the contract.
"We'll be doing all the customer data and billing information systems," Maura O'Neill, ConnexT's president and chief executive officer, told Reuters.

"One of the biggest headaches facing utilities is building up and maintaining customer data systems...We take the technology risk out of the utility (and) amortize this development cost over several million customers," O'Neill said.
O'Neill said the contract was agreed in December but first announced today.
Puget Sound Energy was created by the merger, completed earlier this month, of Washington Energy Co and Puget Sound Power & Light Co.

ConnexT was already providing customer information and billing services to the 500,000 customers Washington Natural Gas Co brought to the merger. The service contract was expanded to include Puget Sound Power & Light's 860,000 electricity customers in western Washington.
ConnexT's services are aimed at utilities seeking greater flexibility and efficiency in customer service as they ready themselves for open competition in a deregulated marketplace.

The company integrates metering and pricing, distribution systems and customer information systems, making it possible to automate meter readings, pricing options, usage warnings and outage notifications.
